subject: Latency and 5xx spike on HorizonLink private deployment

Cc: HorizonLink Ops <ops@horizonlink.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@horizonlink.com>
Date: 2027-05-15T22:17:00Z
Subject: Latency + 5xx surge — private cluster (tag: urgent)

Hi Lauren —

We started seeing a spike in p95 latency and 5xx errors ~21:30 UTC after the rolling update yesterday. Key symptoms: p95 jumped from ~180ms to ~1.2s for text-generation endpoints, and 5xx rate climbed to ~6% for ~35 minutes before partially recovering. Throughput dropped ~18% during the window. This is impacting our inference SLA and a live customer workflow.

Attached logs include a consolidated trace from our edge and a sample error payload. Can you confirm if Redwood pushed any runtime changes or model variant switches to our VPC yesterday? We need a short remediation plan and ETA for stabilization.

Alyssa
Alyssa Turner
Head of Platform Engineering, HorizonLink
alyssa.turner@horizonlink.com

Subject: Re: Latency + 5xx surge — private cluster (tag: urgent)

Alyssa — thanks for the heads up and for the logs. We're treating this as high priority. Short answers up front: we did a lightweight runtime patch (1.4.2) that toggles a new KV-prefetch optimization for VPCs, but that patch was staged only to a canary pool (not your prod pool) per the rollout notes. That said, the symptoms you describe (p95 spike + throughput drop + 5xx burst) match a scenario we've seen when KV cache warmup fails and the system falls back to a heavier decode path.

Plan: Marcus and I will investigate immediately. Next steps I propose: 1) confirm whether your environment got the patch by checking orchestration logs; 2) if there's a model-variant fallback or kernel mismatch, roll back the runtime on affected nodes; 3) warm up KV cache (rerun recent hot prefixes) and temporarily increase reserved concurrency to absorb pressure; 4) follow-up with a short executive note for SLA/credit discussion if the impact window is confirmed.

Can you confirm the exact primaries that saw the 5xx spike (node IDs from your trace)? We may request a short maintenance window to restart a small subset for rollback. Marcus — please triage logs and confirm whether the trace shows repeated KV cache misses or decoder OOMs. Monica — I'll loop you in for postmortem/SLA comms.

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: HorizonLink Ops <ops@horizonlink.com>
Date: 2027-05-15T23:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Latency + 5xx surge — private cluster (tag: urgent)

Lauren / Monica — I pulled the trace Alyssa sent and correlated with our control plane logs. Quick findings:

- Multiple requests show repeated KV cache misses for hot prefixes; downstream we see longer decoder runs (median decode token time ×3).
- A subset of nodes (hln-pri-07 and hln-pri-08) reported transient codec fallback warnings at 21:28 UTC and then a spike in reject/502s at 21:31 UTC.
- No obvious OOMs or GPU saturation on telemetry; GPU utilization actually dips when p95 spikes (indicates blocking in CPU/decoder path).

Hypothesis: the new KV-prefetch code path introduced in runtime 1.4.2 can cause cache invalidation during certain rolling updates when prefix warmup races with request routing. If requests hit a node before warmup completes, they fall back to a slower decode path and can exacerbate queueing, producing increased p95 and downstream 5xx when queue lengths overflow.

Immediate remediation I recommend:
1) Roll back nodes hln-pri-07 and hln-pri-08 to runtime 1.4.1 (we can do a targeted rollback on those two).
2) Rehydrate KV cache by replaying recent hot prefixes (we have a warmup runner that can be scoped to those nodes).
3) Increase reserved concurrency by +20% for the next 45 minutes to blunt queueing while caches rehydrate.
4) Keep an eye on decoder fallback logs for 15 minutes post-rollback; if 5xx persists, escalate to a full pool restart.

I can run the rollback and warmup now if HorizonLink permits a small maintenance window (5–10 minutes).

Alyssa — thanks for reporting and for the trace. Per Marcus' analysis above, the safe path is a targeted rollback + cache warmup. We're ready to proceed as soon as you sign off on a 10-minute maintenance window.

Mutual Action Plan (MAP) — 16 May (hours are UTC):
- T+00 (on sign-off): rollback hln-pri-07 + hln-pri-08 to runtime 1.4.1 (Marcus).
- T+05: start KV cache warmup scoped to top 20 prefixes (Marcus).
- T+15: increase reserved concurrency +20% (Control plane change).
- T+45: monitor p95, 5xx and throughput; if p95 has not declined below 300ms and 5xx remains >1%, escalate to a wider pool restart.
- Postmortem: Redwood and HorizonLink ops to deliver timeline + root cause within 48 hours, and work through possible SLA credit if the measurable impact window exceeds your contract's SLA threshold.

Please reply with OK to proceed and preferred window — if you can do immediate, we'll aim to run the rollback in the next 10 minutes.

Regards,

Subject: Re: Latency + 5xx spike — private cluster (executive summary)

Team — final note for leadership inbox. Short summary for the exec ribbon:

What happened: HorizonLink experienced a 35-minute production incident on 2027-05-15 21:28–22:03 UTC where p95 latency rose to ~1.2s and 5xx rate peaked at ~6% after a rolling update. The immediate cause appears to be a race in the new KV-prefetch optimization introduced in runtime 1.4.2 which allowed requests to land on nodes before warmup completed, triggering decoder fallbacks and queue spikes.

Action taken: Targeted rollback of two affected primaries (hln-pri-07/08) and KV cache rehydration were performed; reserved concurrency was increased to stabilize traffic. Observable impact window: ~21:28–22:03 UTC. Customer-facing actions: Monica initiated MAP and will own SLA follow-up.

Status: Stabilized. Postmortem in flight (48-hour ETA). Recommended follow-ups: 1) hold 1.4.2 rollout and run e2e warmup gating for all VPC rollouts; 2) add TTL checks for prefetched KV entries and a slow-start routing policy for recently-updated nodes; 3) Clarify SLA credit calculation if incident window exceeds threshold.

I will share the postmortem draft and the runbook updates after Marcus finishes the telemetry dive.

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
